name: LLM Token Counter & Cost Estimator API
shortDescription: Approximate token count + exact USD cost for any text and model, from a static pricing table
description: Agent-native, deterministic token and cost estimator computed in real code — no LLM and no upstream calls. Text + model id returns an APPROXIMATE token count (offline heuristic, not the model's real tokenizer) and, when output tokens are supplied, the exact USD cost from a static, versioned pricing table (Anthropic Fable/Opus/Sonnet/Haiku + OpenAI + Google). Unknown models return found:false with null prices — never a guessed number. Token estimates always carry confidence 0.7 and an 'approximate tokenizer' invalidator; cost given a token count is exact. /count handles one text; /lookup adds reasoning, invalidators, recommended actions, chain-to hints, privacy and deterministic execution metadata.

name: Context Window Budget Planner API
shortDescription: Check whether a prompt fits a model's context window and get a deterministic trim plan
description: Agent-native, deterministic context-budget planner computed in real code — no LLM. Given a list of messages (with supplied token counts OR text to estimate), a context window (explicit or derived from a model id), and an output reserve, it returns whether the prompt fits, the overflow, and — if it doesn't fit — a deterministic trim plan that drops the oldest messages or the lowest-priority ones until it fits. Token counts from text are offline heuristic estimates (confidence 0.7); when all token counts are supplied the fit math is exact (confidence 1.0). /plan returns the fit check + trim plan; /lookup adds reasoning, invalidators, recommended actions, chain-to hints, privacy and execution metadata.

name: Text Chunker / Splitter API (RAG)
shortDescription: Split text into RAG chunks by tokens, characters, sentences or paragraphs with exact offsets
description: Agent-native, deterministic text splitter for RAG pipelines computed in real code — no LLM. Splits text by token budget (char-approximated), fixed character windows, sentences, or paragraphs, with configurable overlap, and returns every chunk with exact, gapless character offsets and an estimated token count. Character offsets are exact and reproducible; the tokens strategy approximates token windows at ~4 chars/token and all per-chunk token counts are offline heuristic estimates (carried as invalidators). /chunk returns the chunks; /lookup adds reasoning, invalidators, recommended actions, chain-to hints, privacy and execution metadata.

name: Conversation Cost Ledger API
shortDescription: Tally and price a chat message log, with optional spend projection for N more turns
description: Agent-native, deterministic conversation cost ledger computed in real code — no LLM. Tallies input and output tokens across a message log (supplied tokens or text to estimate), prices them against a static, versioned pricing table, and optionally projects spend for N more turns from observed or supplied per-turn averages. Assistant messages count as output; all other roles count as input. This is a naive per-message tally — real chat APIs re-send prior context as input each turn, so cumulative input cost is higher (stated as an invalidator). Cost given supplied token counts is exact (confidence 1.0); estimated tokens drop confidence to 0.7. /tally returns the ledger; /lookup adds reasoning, invalidators, recommended actions, chain-to hints, privacy and execution metadata.

name: Model Pricing Comparator API
shortDescription: Rank every LLM by exact USD cost for a given input/output token split and call count
description: Agent-native, deterministic LLM pricing comparator computed in real code — no LLM. Given an input/output token split and a call count, it costs every requested model (or the entire static table — Anthropic Fable/Opus/Sonnet/Haiku + OpenAI + Google) and ranks them cheapest-first, reporting per-call and all-calls totals plus savings versus the most expensive option. Because tokens are supplied (not estimated), costs are exact arithmetic against the table — only the snapshot date qualifies them. Unknown requested models are returned in unknown_models, never guessed. /compare returns the ranking; /lookup adds reasoning, invalidators, recommended actions, chain-to hints, privacy and execution metadata.
